analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, לַיַּבָּשָׁה identifies the dry land as what God names, and אֶרֶץ gives it the name “Earth.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיִּקְרָא, “he called.” The masculine singular verb identifies God as the one who named the dry land אֶרֶץ, “earth.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לַיַּבָּשָׁה אֶרֶץ, לַ־ marks the dry land as the entity God names אֶרֶץ. The parallel clause names the gathered waters יַמִּים, “seas.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute noun with prefixed לְ and the definite article, combined as לַ־.

analysis.evidence: God calls the dry land (לַיַּבָּשָׁה) אֶרֶץ and gives the gathered waters the parallel name יַמִּים, “seas.” The naming pair identifies אֶרֶץ as the dry portion.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, usually feminine, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Assign the occurrence to the water sense of מִקְוֶה in tiqvah and make the link to יִקָּווּ explicit in its verse evidence.
draft.definition: A body of water formed as waters gather together.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:10 names the gathered waters “Seas,” following the command for the waters to gather in Genesis 1:9.

analysis.evidence: God calls מִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם, “the gathering of the waters,” יַמִּים, “Seas.” The noun echoes יִקָּווּ in Genesis 1:9, where God commands the waters to gather in one place.
analysis.morphology: וּ־ conjunction “and” + לְ־ preposition “to” + מִקְוֵה, masculine singular construct noun governing הַמַּיִם.

analysis.evidence: In וּלְמִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם קָרָא יַמִּים, the phrase לְמִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם identifies what God named, and יַמִּים (“Seas”) gives the name. This parallels God’s naming the dry land אֶרֶץ (“Earth”) in the preceding clause.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: Just as God calls the dry ground אֶרֶץ, he calls the gathering of the waters (מִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם) יַמִּים. The plural names the gathered waters “seas.”
In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב, אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and כִּי טוֹב gives the content of what God saw: “that it was good.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב, “God saw that it was good,” the singular verb וַיַּרְא takes אֱלֹהִים as its subject. It refers to the same God who named the land and seas earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב, “God saw that it was good,” כִּי introduces the content of what God saw.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected subordinating conjunction without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: After God names the dry land and the seas, וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב means “God saw that it was good.” טוֹב expresses God’s judgment of what he saw.
analysis.morphology: Predicative adjective, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
